experiment.claim: Substantiates spec/target-spec.md's ratified "Stability" row (stable 0-50 mA over the ratified C_out/ESR window; PM >= 45 deg, GM >= 10 dB worst corner) against the issue-#25 current-mirror-OTA revision of the LDO core-regulation loop (design/ldo_3v3in_1v8out.sch). Both the spec row and the window are ratified by issue #1 / DR-006 -- the window being DR-002's C_eff 0.33-4.7 uF / ESR 0-500 mOhm / no-minimum-ESR posture -- so the bounds below cite them verbatim rather than an invented final limit. What DR-002 ratified is the window's numeric boundaries; its no-minimum-ESR *stability claim* is only partially substantiated, per DR-006's own disclosed 0 mA-corner gap, which is exactly what this testbench measures. This is also the testbench DR-002 sequenced itself in front of: DR-002 states its no-minimum-ESR posture stays an unverified claim 'until a loop-gain sim/ record exists', and names the low-C_eff/low-ESR corner as the one that has to be shown. Method: closed-loop injection at VREF with the loop gain recovered as T = X/(1-X), X = v(xldo.fb) -- see the testbench schematic's header for the derivation, and for the one approximation it makes (input-pair path asymmetry, a fraction of a degree at these crossovers). As of #179 all seven points are seeded per sim/README.md's initial-condition contract (#171): the testbench carries a .nodeset card seeding the three branch-defining nodes (VOUT=1.8, FB=1.2, N_FBB=0.6), which ngspice applies to EVERY operating-point solve in the deck -- including the one each `ac` performs for itself -- so no point linearizes around an unconstrained Newton solve. `.ic` would not have done this: ngspice honours `.ic` only for the transient operating point, so it is inert in an ac-only deck. Only the branch-defining nodes are seeded, because a .nodeset card is a single static card applied to all seven points while every other node's value is set by the operating current: the eleven-node seed from sim/ic-screen-125c-b (125C/50mA values) was measured to drag ss/-40C/3.63V's 1mA point onto a non-regulating branch (VOUT=3.633V=VIN) and to raise solver diagnostics on 9 of 45 corners, where the three-node seed raises none of the former and fewer of the latter -- see sim/README.md's "#179". The seed does NOT clear #171's solver-diagnostic FAIL gate; the residue is recorded as a finding there, not suppressed.
